Describes the GPU and the machine an app runs on, from its panel or from the

238.name: diagnose
238.docs:
Finds the GPU the way a window would and describes it, along with the machine
and the build, without showing anything. For a command line option such as
`--diagnostics`, which still answers when a window would not open or would be
too slow to use. Printing the result gives text to paste into a bug report.

Call it instead of running the app: a process has only one event loop.

10.name: access
10.docs:
Screen reader support: the UI's [`AccessTree`] translated to AccessKit,
which talks to VoiceOver on macOS, Narrator and NVDA on Windows, and Orca
on Linux.

1064.name: ravenrs_platform_native
1064.docs:
Desktop backend for RavenRS: one winit window per app, rendered with wgpu
(Metal on macOS, DX12/Vulkan on Windows, Vulkan/GL on Linux).

Frames are produced on demand: the event loop sleeps until input arrives or
reactive state changes, so an idle app uses no CPU or GPU time.

Screen readers see the UI through AccessKit: the accessibility tree is
built only while one is running.

and the tree changed.
